spec.objective: EDIT the existing pyproject.toml in the external NobleGreedv2 repo to add a [tool.pytest.ini_options] table pinning testpaths = ["tests"], so bare pytest from the repo root collects ONLY the tests/ tree instead of walking the whole repo (corpus/target fixtures and unbuilt *_wired.py oracles) and emitting ~190 ModuleNotFoundError collection errors.
functional_requirements: Append a new [tool.pytest.ini_options] table after [tool.setuptools] carrying the single key testpaths = ["tests"] (a one-element array), with a trailing newline after the last line and nothing else (no comments, no extra blank lines, no extra keys).
Retain every pre-existing line of pyproject.toml verbatim and in order: the [build-system], [project], and [tool.setuptools] tables are unchanged.

Emit the edit as a single top-level __JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__ dict with EXACTLY ONE entry keyed 'pyproject.toml' whose value is the verbatim whole-file final content (table headers starting at column 0, no leading indentation), and no other top-level statement.
Add no pytest ini key other than testpaths, and set testpaths to exactly the single-element ["tests"] — so tests is the SOLE configured collection root.
spec.interfaces:
The whole-file final content of pyproject.toml MUST be EXACTLY:

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "ngv2"
version = "0.0.0"
requires-python = ">=3.10"

[tool.setuptools]
packages = ["ngv2"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]

(with a trailing newline after the last line). When parsed by tomllib it MUST yield data["tool"]["pytest"]["ini_options"]["testpaths"] == ["tests"] while retaining the [build-system], [project], and [tool.setuptools] tables unchanged.

NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.


# COMMITTED ORACLE CONTRACT (authoritative; you cannot read these files at synthesis time so they are reproduced verbatim -- your code MUST make them pass):

## tests/ngv2/test_pytest_testpaths_wired.py
```python
"""RED oracle — pyproject.toml must pin pytest ``testpaths = ["tests"]``.

Contract (verified live 2026-06-11):
  NGv2 pyproject.toml has NO ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]`` table, so bare
  ``pytest`` from the repo root has no configured collection root. It then
  walks the whole tree (corpus/target fixtures and unbuilt ``*_wired.py``
  oracles), producing ~190 ModuleNotFoundError collection errors.

The fix pins the suite scope to the single ``tests`` directory:

    [tool.pytest.ini_options]
    testpaths = ["tests"]

These tests are RED today (the key is absent → KeyError surfaced as an
assertion failure). They flip GREEN once the stanza lands. Stdlib only:
``tomllib`` parses the TOML; no third-party packaging/config library.
"""

import tomllib

from pathlib import Path

# Derive the repo root from this file's own path (tests/ngv2/<this file>),
# never from CWD.
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
PYPROJECT = REPO_ROOT / "pyproject.toml"

EXPECTED_TESTPATHS = ["tests"]


def _load_pyproject() -> dict:
    """Parse pyproject.toml at the repo root via stdlib tomllib."""
    with PYPROJECT.open("rb") as fh:
        return tomllib.load(fh)


def _ini_options(data: dict) -> dict:
    """The [tool.pytest.ini_options] table, or {} if any level is absent."""
    return data.get("tool", {}).get("pytest", {}).get("ini_options", {})


def test_pyproject_file_exists_at_repo_root():
    assert PYPROJECT.is_file(), f"missing pyproject.toml at {PYPROJECT}"


def test_pyproject_parses_as_toml():
    # Guards against a malformed edit; GREEN today (file is valid TOML).
    assert isinstance(_load_pyproject(), dict)


def test_pytest_ini_options_table_present():
    data = _load_pyproject()
    assert "ini_options" in data.get("tool", {}).get("pytest", {}), (
        "pyproject.toml must declare a [tool.pytest.ini_options] table"
    )


def test_testpaths_pinned_to_tests():
    data = _load_pyproject()
    assert data["tool"]["pytest"]["ini_options"]["testpaths"] == EXPECTED_TESTPATHS, (
        "pyproject.toml must pin [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths == [\"tests\"] "
        "so bare `pytest` collects only the tests/ tree"
    )


def test_tests_is_only_collection_root_wired():
    """Wiring anchor: ``tests`` is the SOLE configured collection root.

    A single-element testpaths is what actually narrows bare-`pytest`
    collection to tests/ on the live repo; more than one root (or none)
    would re-admit the corpus/target trees and the unbuilt *_wired oracles.
    """
    testpaths = _ini_options(_load_pyproject()).get("testpaths", [])
    assert testpaths == EXPECTED_TESTPATHS, (
        "testpaths must be exactly [\"tests\"] — the only collection root; "
        f"got {testpaths!r}"
    )
    assert len(testpaths) == 1 and testpaths[0] == "tests", (
        "exactly one collection root ('tests') must be configured"
    )

```
